newsitem.title: CONGO: Mobutu arrives for Zairean peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu arrives for Zairean peace talks.

text.p: President Mobutu Sese Seko arrived in the Congolese port of Pointe Noire on Wednesday for a second round of face-to-face talks with his rebel rival, Laurent Kabila, on a South African ship docked there, witnesses said.
South African President Nelson Mandela arrived earlier to chair the meeting aboard the navy icebreaker Outeniqua and a helicopter left the ship around noon (1100 GMT) apparently to fetch Kabila.
The talks had been expected to start at 11 a.m., but were delayed by the late arrival of the participants.

South African Defence Minister Joe Modise told reporters shortly before the talks began that Pretoria was hopeful of a breakthrough to end Zaire's seven-month civil war and ensure a smooth transition to democracy.
"There's no reason why we should not expect a breakthrough. That's why we're here," he said moments before he flew off in the ship's helicopter to fetch Kabila from a nearby port.

Kabila, whose forces have been closing in on the capital, has been insisting, in public at least, that Mobutu must hand over power at the meeting. Mobutu has insisted he will only surrender power to an elected successor.
